reason: The text emphasizes hierarchical relationships throughout. God establishes clear authority structures: God commands a prophet, who addresses Israel; God directly commissions Gideon as leader; Gideon commands his men with explicit instructions ('from me you shall see and so you shall do' - 'מִמֶּנִּי תִרְא֖וּ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ'). The military organization is strictly hierarchical: three companies with leaders, coordinated commands, and men explicitly following Gideon's example. Even when the narrative emphasizes that victory comes from God rather than military might, this does not discourage hierarchy—it establishes that hierarchy operates under divine authority. The text presents structured authority as essential to accomplishing God's purposes.
